protocol: Three fresh Chrome processes per backend and model; rotated/reversed backend order; original published cameras and full PLY/SH3 inputs; rendering settings adjusted as closely as possible; camera-axis sorting; GSL default sorting only; one frame in flight; native GPU timestamps. PlayCanvas Engine 2.23.0-beta.20 uses large on WebGL2 and WebGPU. Additional static/moving raw stochastic cases compare PlayCanvas WebGPU native blue noise, SuperSplat and both GSL backends. Spatial resolve is measured for SuperSplat and GSL; all temporal accumulation is disabled. Post-GC main and live Worker V8 heaps are sampled before instrumentation traversal; external backing and WASM capacity remain separate. SuperSplat 3.4.2 adds its native WebGPU renderer, fixed minPixelSize 2, native stochastic depth occlusion enabled and motion-adaptive contribution culling disabled, and raw stochastic plus spatial resolve with warp disabled. Moving cases use a frame-stepped sinusoidal orbit with 45 degrees amplitude on either side of the base view, matching the lab amplitude.
